name: cure2fewshot
description: Code, frozen annotations and expected outputs for a deterministic protocol that converts a public pill image collection into a few shot retrieval benchmark aligned with the published low shot evaluation protocol of ePillID, together with a scored rubric that decides whether the converted result is fit for use. This deposit contains no image. The image collection must be obtained from its original authors at https://github.com/suiyiling/Few-shot-pill-recognition and is not redistributed here, nor is any image derived from it. What is released is the protocol's own annotations about publicly distributed files: a bounding box manifest of 8811 crops, the near duplicate leakage list, the flagged duplicate label pairs and the merge decisions, plus the scripts that turn those into splits, measurements and a rubric score. Applied to the CURE collection the protocol yields 8811 crops over 390 classes, a gallery of 386 references and 8423 queries, with zero measured leakage. The rubric scores the direct conversion at 80 out of 100, capped to the middle band because the two image sources are not materially separated, and the hardened conversion at 92, accepted as a primary benchmark. The release also ships the earlier, defective variant of the background hardening mask, whose threshold cut into pale tablets. That variant scores 100 out of 100, higher than the corrected one, because damaging the reference object inflates the very separation the rubric rewards.
